response.rationale: The history of caterpillar hair keratitis (F05) and the characteristic brown multilobular deep stromal lesions (F09) without epithelial defect (F10) strongly suggest ophthalmia nodosa, despite prior resolution (F06). The DSAEK (F03) may have triggered a delayed reaction, with onset 2 months postoperatively (F07). Other infectious keratitides are less likely given the absence of epithelial defect and typical signs, and the deep stromal involvement on AS-OCT (F11, F12) supports a granulomatous process rather than a surface infection.
